name: GaddaFix — Telangana Pothole Operations Platform (gadda = pothole in Telugu; working name "RoadFix-TG")
one_paragraph_pitch: GaddaFix turns TGSRTC buses and GHMC/R&B vehicles into a continuous road-survey fleet: a cheap Android phone or Jetson box runs a YOLO26 segmentation model on the vehicle, uploads only pothole crops + GPS/IMU (<1 GB/bus/month), and a GPU server computes metric depth, area and volume per pothole by fitting the road plane to a monocular metric depth map and integrating the mask below it, scale-locked by the known camera mounting height. Detections from many passes are map-matched and clustered into one confirmed pothole, graded by IRC:82-2015 severity (25/50 mm depth, 200/500 mm width), scored for priority with configurable weights (severity, exposure, vulnerability of nearby schools/hospitals/bus stops, age vs SLA, monsoon), and converted automatically into a cold-mix work order (IRC:116 / IRC:SP:100 material spec, bags of 25/50 kg, cost estimate, square-cut dimensions) routed to the owning agency (GHMC/Cyberabad MC/Malkajgiri MC/R&B/NHAI/Cantonment) and the responsible CRMP contractor with its SLA and defect-liability period. The same bus cameras then verify the repair (N clean passes auto-closes the order), reopen it if the patch fails inside the DLP (contractor liable, no pay), and feed Telugu/Hindi/English ward and zone dashboards, citizen-complaint merging (MyCURE/WhatsApp), measurement-book export and a full audit trail. Everything is runnable today on the dev box with RDD2022-India, eYantra Indian-road masks, public TGSRTC GTFS and OSM Hyderabad data, and nothing requires Docker.
architecture:
## 0. Components at a glance (data flow left to right)

[Edge capture: bus/van phone or Jetson] --(crops + meta, store-and-forward)--> [Ingest API, FastAPI] --> [MinIO/S3 object store + PostgreSQL 18/PostGIS 3.6] --> [Celery GPU worker: seg verify -> depth -> plane -> volume] --> [Geo worker: map-match -> dedup cluster -> pothole entity] --> [Ops engine: IRC severity -> priority score -> repair plan -> work order -> SLA/DLP state machine] --> [Verification worker: clean-pass auto-close, recurrence watch] --> [React/MapLibre PWA dashboards (te/hi/en), field app, contractor portal, citizen portal] + [Citizen complaint intake (web form, WhatsApp webhook stub)] + [Audit log on every state change]

Tenancy: `agency` table (GHMC, Cyberabad MC, Malkajgiri MC, Telangana R&B, HMDA, NHAI, SCB). Every road segment, pothole, work order and user is scoped by `agency_id`; admin hierarchy table `admin_unit(kind in zone|circle|ward|division, geom)` is pluggable (loaded from GeoJSON; GHMC 6 zones/30 circles/150 wards today, swappable when the 300-ward re-delimitation lands).

## 1. Edge capture (two tiers, same wire protocol)

Tier A (TSRTC buses, municipal garbage trucks; ~Rs 12-20k/vehicle): Android phone (Rs 8-12k, Snapdragon 6xx+), CameraX 1.5, LiteRT GPU delegate FP16, model `yolo26n-seg` exported with `model.export(format="litert", quantize=16)`; fixed-focus, 1/500 s exposure cap, 1280x720 @ 30 fps, windshield mount at measured height h (tape, stored in config). Trigger a keyframe only when haversine(last_fix, now) >= 4 m and speed >= 5 km/h; run the model; when any pothole mask with conf >= 0.35 appears, package: 1280px JPEG keyframe (q=80), mask polygons, bbox, conf, GPS fix (lat, lon, accuracy_m, heading, speed), 200 ms IMU window (accel z-jolt magnitude), camera_id, h, pitch, trip_id, monotonic timestamp. Store in Room/SQLite queue, upload via resumable multipart to `/v1/ingest/observations` on depot Wi-Fi or 4G. For the demo the edge is simulated by `edge/sim_bus.py`: it replays an RDD2022-India image sequence (or any dashcam MP4) along a TGSRTC GTFS route shape (mdb-3361) with synthetic GPS noise (sigma 6 m) and posts observations exactly as the phone would.

Tier B (GHMC/R&B inspection vans, 1-2 per zone; ~Rs 1.2-1.5 lakh): Jetson Orin Nano Super on an industrial carrier (RDP CARINA / Seeed J3011, 60 C rated) + global-shutter 2 MP camera, optional ZED 2i or OAK-D for stereo ground truth; runs `yolo26s-seg` TensorRT FP16 and uploads full-res frames; its stereo depth is used to calibrate and audit Tier A volumes and for contractor billing.

Hard edge requirements: 24 V -> 5 V isolated DC-DC, ignition-off flush, shaded mount, thermal throttle guard (stop inference above 45 C battery temp), NavIC/L5 GNSS when available, every fix carries `accuracy_m` (down-weighted above 15 m).

## 2. Server detection and segmentation (verifier/teacher)

Models (all downloadable now):
- Edge/primary: Ultralytics YOLO26 seg (`yolo26n-seg.pt` / `yolo26s-seg.pt` from the `Ultralytics/YOLO26` HF repo or GitHub releases; ultralytics 8.4.211; AGPL-3.0 - note Enterprise licence for production govt deployment, or swap to RF-DETR Seg Apache-2.0 which the pipeline supports through a common `Segmenter` interface).
- Server verifier/teacher: `rfdetr` RF-DETR Seg-Small (Apache 2.0), used to re-score uploaded crops and to pseudo-label Hyderabad data collected later.
- Bootstrap weights for day-1 demo before our fine-tune finishes: `vinothvikas1987/pothole-detection-yolov8` (Apache 2.0, best.pt) or `mfranzon/pothole-yolo26` via `hf_hub_download`.

Training data (demo-feasible):
- RDD2022 India zip (CC BY-SA 4.0, 502 MB, 7,706 train imgs, 3,187 D40 pothole boxes) -> converted to YOLO; classes mapped to {pothole (D40), crack (D00+D10+D20 merged), (optional) manhole/speed_breaker negatives}.
- eYantra "Semantic Segmentation Dataset of Indian Roads" (Kaggle `eyantraiit/semantic-segmentation-datasets-of-indian-roads`, 3,227 imgs, pothole + road masks, GPL-2 so prototype only) -> YOLO seg polygons; gives the mask supervision and a road-mask head.
- Optional: BharatPotHole (Kaggle, verify licence), Roboflow `vnr-project/pothole-segmentation-8esmn` (possibly Hyderabad).
- Box-only RDD images get masks via a SAM-style box prompt pass (we use the seg model trained on eYantra to pseudo-mask RDD boxes, then a second round of training; keeps the stack Apache/Ultralytics only).
- Negatives: manholes, shadows, speed breakers, wet patches from IDD (IIIT-H, Hyderabad scenes, no pothole class) sampled as background images to cut false positives.
Training recipe: `yolo26s-seg`, imgsz 960, 80 epochs, mosaic + HSV + rain/blur albumentations, class weights for D10; eval mAP50 on RDD-India D40 + mask IoU on eYantra test. Target: box mAP50 >= 0.75 pothole, mask IoU >= 0.70. Export: `onnx` + `engine` (TensorRT FP16 for the dev RTX 5080) + `litert` INT8/FP16 for Android.

## 3. Depth and volume (hard requirement) - see depth_method field for formulas

Server-side per observation: undistort with stored intrinsics -> `depth-anything/DA3METRIC-LARGE` (Apache 2.0, metric mono depth, focal-aware) with fallback `depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Metric-VKITTI-Base` -> back-project -> RANSAC road plane on road pixels (excluding pothole masks) in the 3-12 m band -> height-lock scale s = h_true/h_hat -> per-pixel depth below plane -> area, max depth, p95 depth, volume -> IRC:82 severity -> multi-frame fusion across the track (BoT-SORT ids inside one trip, then cluster-level fusion across passes). Water-filled detection: RGB detector fires but depth-below-plane < 8 mm and specular/sky-reflection score high -> `water_filled=true, depth=unknown`, prioritised by area + complaints + IMU jolt. Confidence intervals are stored with every measurement (per-distance-bin error model, re-fitted from Tier B stereo/inspector ground truth).

## 4. Geolocation and dedup

- Map matching: OSRM `/match` for the demo (built from Geofabrik southern-zone extract clipped to Telangana bbox with osmium; no docker: osrm-backend binary built from source or prebuilt; fallback: nearest-way with heading filter via PostGIS `<->` on an `osm_ways` table, which is what the demo ships with to avoid the build). Production: Valhalla Meili.
- Position of the pothole (not the camera): project the mask centroid through the calibrated camera onto the fitted road plane -> (X forward, Y lateral) in metres -> offset from the GPS fix along `heading` -> pothole lat/lon, plus `lane_offset_m` from the lane centre.
- Dedup key: (`way_id`, heading bucket 90 deg, H3 res-12 cell) then DBSCAN (eps 6 m haversine, min_samples 2) over the rolling 30-day window inside the same way+direction and `|lane_offset diff| < 1.5 m` -> `pothole` entity; each detection stays an `observation`. Status: `candidate` (1 pass) -> `confirmed` (>= 2 passes from >= 2 trips, or 1 pass + citizen complaint within 25 m) -> dispatch-eligible. Citizen complaints (MyCURE-style form, WhatsApp webhook with photo + location) enter the same clustering with `source='citizen'`.

## 5. Prioritisation (configurable per agency/zone, stored in `priority_config` JSONB, versioned)

P = 100 * (wS*S + wE*E + wV*V + wT*T + wM*M), defaults wS=0.30, wE=0.25, wV=0.20, wT=0.15, wM=0.10.
- S severity (IRC:82-2015 cl. 7.5.3.4): depth > 50 mm or width > 500 mm -> 1.0; 25-50 mm / 200-500 mm -> 0.6; below -> 0.3; +0.2 if in wheel path (|lane_offset| < 1.2 m) or within 30 m of a junction; water_filled -> treated as 0.8 pending measurement; capped at 1.0.
- E exposure: OSM highway class (trunk/primary 1.0, secondary 0.8, tertiary 0.6, residential 0.4) * (1 + 0.5*min(1, bus_routes_through_way/5)) * (1 + 0.5*min(1, passes_per_day/50)), normalised to 1.
- V vulnerability: 1 - prod(1 - v_i) over POIs within 200 m: school 0.5, hospital 0.5, bus stop (GTFS) 0.3, metro station 0.3, market 0.2; +0.2 if unlit (OSM lit=no) .
- T age: min(1, days_since_confirmed / sla_days) with +0.3 once SLA breached; cumulative citizen complaints add min(0.3, 0.1*n).
- M monsoon: 1.0 normally; 1.3 during declared monsoon window (Jun-Sep, Oct-Nov NE) or 72-h rain > 30 mm (IMD district feed, mocked in demo); 1.5 if pothole lies in a registered waterlogging hotspot polygon.
Also computed per stretch: IRC:82 Table 5.3 urban rating (pothole % area > 0.5 -> Poor) for 100 m segments, feeding ward/zone "road health" tiles.

## 6. Repair planning module (cold mix, IRC:116 / IRC:SP:100 / IRC:82 Sec 10)

Inputs: fused A (m2), bbox L x W (m), d_avg, d_max, water_filled. Steps:
1. Square cut: L_cut = L + 0.25, W_cut = W + 0.25 (100-150 mm margin each side, IRC:82 11.4 "cut adjoining deteriorated portion"); A_cut = L_cut * W_cut.
2. Design depth d_design = max(d_avg, 0.050) rounded up to 5 mm; if d_design > 0.075 -> layered: base layers of 25-75 mm with Crusher Run Macadam (d_design - 0.050) + 50 mm patching mix on top (IRC:116 cl 5.2).
3. Volumes: V_patch = A_cut * min(d_design, 0.075 if single layer else 0.050); V_crm = A_cut * max(0, d_design - 0.050).
4. Mass_patch = V_patch * 2200 kg/m3 (compacted) * (1 + wastage 0.12) ; bags_25 = ceil(Mass/25) (or 50 kg per IRC:116 default); CRM tonnes = V_crm * 2.1.
5. Tack/prime: 0.30 kg/m2 SS-1 / CSS-1 emulsion on A_cut; sand 1 kg/m2 blinding.
6. Labour: 2 mazdoor-hours per pothole base + 1 h per extra 0.25 m3; equipment: jet patcher recommended when cluster of >= 8 potholes within 300 m or any single pothole > 1 m2; infrared recommended for water_filled when a Road Doctor unit is available in the zone.
7. Cost = bags * unit_cost_bag (default Rs 350/25 kg, editable rate table per agency/year with MoRTH SDB 2019 item codes) + emulsion kg * Rs 45 + CRM t * Rs 1,100 + labour h * Rs 100 + 10% T&P; shows side-by-side with historical benchmark (GHMC Rs 7,396/pothole reported 2021) and the cuboid overestimate (L x W x d_max) to make material savings visible.
8. Material spec string on the work order: "IRC:116-2014 readymade cut-back mix (MC-800), 4.5-5.5 % residual bitumen" (storable, monsoon) or "IRC:SP:100-2014 emulsion cold mix SS-2, 7-8 % emulsion" per agency preference; weather rule: patching allowed in damp holes after bailing water (IRC:82 Sec 10), blocked in active rain; finish 10 mm proud (hand) / 3 mm (roller).
Work orders are batched by circle into "repair runs" (greedy route ordering along a nearest-neighbour path on the road graph) with total bags, CRM, emulsion and crew-hours so a DEE can issue one indent per day per circle.

## 7. Work orders, contracts, SLAs, DLP, verification loop

State machine (every transition writes `audit_log` with actor, before/after JSON, reason, lat/lon of the action when from the field app):
candidate -> confirmed -> planned (repair plan attached) -> work_order_issued (contractor, package, sla_due) -> acknowledged -> in_progress (crew check-in, before photo geo+time stamped, bag batch no.) -> repaired_claimed (after photo, actual bags used) -> verification_pending -> verified_closed (>= 3 clean vehicle passes within 14 days AND 10 % random engineer QC sample passed, or engineer manual QC) | reopened (re-detection at same cluster within DLP: patch warranty 6 months or CRMP 5-year package -> contractor liable, rework WO at zero pay, debit note draft) -> recurrence_watch (12 months).
SLA defaults (editable): arterial 24 h (GHMC Citizen's Charter 2023), other roads 72 h in monsoon, 7 days otherwise; R&B state roads 7 days; breach timers drive escalation (AE -> DEE -> EE -> Zonal Commissioner) with notification stubs (email/SMS/WhatsApp adapter interface).
Contract linkage: `contract(package, agency, contractor, road_geoms, start, end, dlp_months, sla_rules)` loaded from CRMP package list (7 packages, LB Nagar/BSCPL etc. as seed); each `road_segment` resolves to its owning agency and current contract by spatial join; unknown owner -> routed to a "jurisdiction queue" (addresses the GHMC/R&B/NHAI/SCB confusion from the Cyberabad CCTV pilot).
Payment linkage (eMARG pattern): measurement-book CSV/PDF generated from estimated vs actual quantities; invoices can only reference `verified_closed` WOs; contractor scorecard = on-time %, recurrence %, QC-fail %, volume variance.

## 8. Dashboards and apps (React 19 + Vite + MapLibre 6 PWA, i18next te/hi/en, Noto Sans Telugu/Devanagari)

- Zonal/circle dashboard: map (PMTiles base + MVT pothole layer from PostGIS ST_AsMVT, H3 heat at low zoom), KPIs (open by severity, SLA breaches, median repair days, bags consumed, Rs saved vs cuboid), ward league table, monsoon mode toggle, IRC stretch rating overlay, contractor scorecards, DLP reopen list.
- Engineer field PWA: offline work-order list for the circle (Dexie/IndexedDB), navigation link, before/after capture with client-side resize to 1280 px, bag count entry, background sync (Workbox); Telugu-first UI.
- Contractor portal: assigned WOs, SLA clock, upload proof, invoice-eligible list.
- Citizen page: report form (photo + GPS), status tracker by ticket, public per-ward transparency counts.
- Admin: priority weights editor, SLA rules, rate tables, ward GeoJSON upload, camera calibration registry, model version registry, audit log viewer, exports (GeoJSON/CSV/measurement book, ArcGIS Field Maps compatible GeoJSON).

## 9. Backend stack
FastAPI 0.162.5 + uvicorn, SQLAlchemy 2.0.x (pin < 2.1 for GeoAlchemy2 0.21 safety) + Alembic, PostgreSQL 18 + PostGIS 3.6 (native install), Redis 8 + Celery 5.7 (`gpu` queue, pool=solo, batch 16 frames), MinIO single binary via boto3, PyJWT + argon2 RBAC (citizen, field_engineer, contractor, zonal_admin, super_admin; row scope by agency_id/zone_id), torch 2.12 cu130, ultralytics 8.4.211, rfdetr, transformers, opencv-python-headless, open3d (RANSAC) with a numpy fallback, shapely/pyproj/h3/scikit-learn. A dedicated Python 3.12 venv for ML workers if any wheel (tensorrt, rfdetr) lags on 3.14; the API stays on 3.14.

Key APIs (all under /v1, JWT, gzip/brotli): POST /ingest/observations (multipart, idempotent by client_uuid); POST /ingest/complaints; GET /potholes?bbox&status&severity&admin_unit&min_priority; GET /potholes/{id} (observations, measurements, plan, WO timeline); GET /tiles/potholes/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt; POST /potholes/{id}/plan (recompute with overrides); POST /work-orders (from pothole ids or auto-run for circle); PATCH /work-orders/{id}/transition; POST /work-orders/{id}/photos; GET /runs/{date}/{circle} (indent: bags, CRM, emulsion, crew); GET /kpi/{admin_unit}?window; GET /contractors/{id}/scorecard; GET /exports/measurement-book.csv|geojson; GET/PUT /admin/priority-config, /admin/rate-table, /admin/sla; POST /admin/admin-units (GeoJSON upload); GET /audit?entity; GET /public/wards (transparency, no auth). ML internal: POST /ml/segment, /ml/measure (used by workers and the demo notebook).

## 10. Verification loop and analytics
Verification worker runs nightly and on each trip ingest: for each WO in verification_pending, count trips passing within 15 m of the cluster along the same way/direction with no detection -> clean_passes; >= 3 within 14 days -> auto-closed (unless QC-sample flagged). Recurrence watcher: new cluster within 6 m of a closed pothole -> dlp_event; reopen with contractor liability if inside DLP. Analytics: per-ward/zone repair-time distributions, recurrence rate per contractor and per material spec (evidence for the "permanent fix" claim), bags consumed vs estimated (volume calibration drift), monsoon spike curves, IRC stretch rating trend, model drift (confidence histogram, FP rate from engineer rejects feeding the retraining set).

## 11. Hardware bill (bus kit Tier A): Android phone Rs 10k, mount/shade/fan Rs 1.5k, 24 V DC-DC Rs 800, IoT SIM Rs 100/month; Tier B van: Orin Nano Super + industrial carrier Rs 75-90k, GS camera Rs 8k, optional ZED 2i Rs 62k, u-blox GNSS Rs 6k. Depot calibration kit: A2 checkerboard 9x6 30 mm, 4 cones, tape, one iPhone Pro (LiDAR) per zone for inspector ground truth.

depth_method:
Goal: metric depth, area and volume of each pothole from a single forward-looking vehicle camera, with error bars, good enough to (a) bin IRC:82-2015 severity (25 mm / 50 mm depth, 200 / 500 mm width) and (b) estimate cold-mix quantity within about 20-25 % after multi-frame fusion.

1. Calibration (once per camera model + 10 min per vehicle): OpenCV calibrateCamera with a 9x6 checkerboard (30 mm squares, A2) -> K = [fx, fy, cx, cy] and distortion k1-k3, p1-p2 (reprojection < 0.3 px, fixed focus). Extrinsics at the depot: tape-measure camera height h_true (bus 2.3-2.5 m, car 1.4 m), place 4 cones at 3/5/8/12 m -> solvePnP -> pitch, roll, yaw. Store in `camera` with a calibration certificate. Online self-check per trip: vanishing point from lane markings (pitch/yaw), lane-width prior 3.5 m +- 0.25 on marked arterials (roll/height), and the plane-fit height drift alert (> 5 %).

2. Depth map: undistort frame; run `depth-anything/DA3METRIC-LARGE` (Apache 2.0) with the calibrated focal: metric_depth_raw = fx_px * net_out / 300 (validate the convention on a cone of known height at 5 m on day 1; if it deviates, fall back to treating the output as relative and rely on step 4). Fallback model: `depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Metric-VKITTI-Base`. Edge/ONNX option: `onnx-community/metric3d-vit-small` (BSD).

3. Back-projection: for pixel (u,v) with depth Z: X = (u-cx)Z/fx, Y = (v-cy)Z/fy, point p = (X,Y,Z).

4. Road plane and scale lock: take road pixels (seg road mask or everything in the lower image band 3-12 m ahead) minus dilated pothole masks; RANSAC plane n.p + d = 0 (threshold 15 mm, 1000 iters, open3d segment_plane or numpy). Estimated camera height h_hat = |d|/|n|. Scale factor s = h_true / h_hat; multiply all Z by s (this cancels most monocular scale error and ties the measurement to a tape-measured quantity; this is the Gamma-from-Mono idea). Record plane RMSE (reject frame if > 25 mm or pitch inconsistent with calibration by > 3 deg).

5. Per-pixel pothole depth: for each pixel in the pothole mask, delta_i = max(0, signed distance of p_i below the plane) = max(0, -(n.p_i + d)/|n|). Pixel ground footprint a_i = (Z_i/fx) * (Z_i/fy) / cos(theta_i) where theta_i is the angle between the viewing ray and the plane normal (equivalent to an inverse-perspective-mapping footprint).

6. Per-frame metrics: area A = sum a_i (over mask); depth_max = max delta_i (robust: 99th percentile); depth_p95; depth_mean = sum(delta_i a_i)/A; volume V = sum delta_i * a_i. Width/length: PCA of the ground-projected mask footprint. Distance D = median Z of mask.

7. Multi-frame fusion: within a trip, track the pothole with BoT-SORT; weight each frame by w = 1/(sigma_D^2) with sigma_D = base_mm * (D/5 m)^2 (base 8 mm at 5 m, from the error model), and discard frames with D > 12 m or mask area < 400 px; fused depth/area/volume are weighted medians; CI from weighted MAD. Across passes (cluster level), fuse pass-level estimates the same way; store `ci_json`. Expected accuracy (to be validated, flagged uncertain): single frame +-10-25 mm depth, +-30-40 % volume; fused +-5-15 mm, +-15-25 %.

8. Water-filled potholes: if the detector fires but depth_p95 < 8 mm and the mask has high specular/sky-reflection score (brightness and low texture), set water_filled = true, depth = unknown, keep area; priority uses area + complaints + IMU jolt; re-measure on next dry pass.

9. Severity mapping (IRC:82-2015 cl. 7.5.3.4): Large if depth_p95 > 50 mm or width > 500 mm; Medium if 25-50 mm or width 200-500 mm; Small otherwise; plus cracks tracked separately (D00/D20) for stretch rating.

10. Repair quantities (IRC:82 Sec 10, IRC:116, IRC:SP:100): cut L_cut = L + 0.25 m, W_cut = W + 0.25 m; d_design = max(depth_mean_over_cut, 50 mm) rounded up to 5 mm; if d_design > 75 mm: CRM sub-base (d_design - 50 mm) + 50 mm patching mix; V_patch = A_cut * d_patch; Mass = V_patch * 2200 kg/m3 * 1.12; bags = ceil(Mass / 25 kg) (50 kg option per IRC:116); emulsion tack 0.3 kg/m2 of A_cut; sand 1 kg/m2. Worked example: pothole 0.50 x 0.40 m, mean depth 60 mm -> cut 0.75 x 0.65 = 0.4875 m2, d_design 60 mm, V = 0.02925 m3, mass 72 kg -> 3 bags of 25 kg (~Rs 1,050 material), 0.15 kg emulsion, ~2 mazdoor-hours; all-in about Rs 1,800 vs the Rs 7,396/pothole GHMC figure reported in 2021 and vs the cuboid method (L x W x d_max) that over-orders 2-4x.

11. Ground truth and audit: inspectors measure 50-100 potholes with straightedge + depth gauge (IRC manual method) and phone LiDAR (iPhone Pro, ~5 % volume error) per zone; Tier B stereo vans (ZED 2i, ~12 % depth error at 40 km/h) provide continuous audit; `ml/depth/validate.py` reports depth MAE and volume MAPE per distance bin and per camera, and re-fits the per-bin sigma used in fusion. Demo on the dev box: the pipeline runs on RDD2022-India images with the default car calibration (h 1.4 m) and on a synthetic "digital pothole" test (render a known bowl into a planar road image) to unit-test the integration maths before real ground truth exists.
key_tradeoffs:
1. Monocular (Tier A) vs stereo (Tier B): mono is Rs 12-20k per bus and fleet-scalable but 15-25 % volume error after fusion and blind on water-filled holes; stereo is 5x costlier and needs Jetson, but gives billing-grade depth within 8 m. We use mono for coverage/prioritisation and stereo + inspector/LiDAR ground truth for calibration and payment, with the work order showing which tier measured it.
2. YOLO26 (AGPL, fastest on edge, NMS-free LiteRT export) vs RF-DETR Seg (Apache 2.0, better domain shift). Pipeline exposes one Segmenter interface; demo trains YOLO26 for edge and RF-DETR as server verifier; production licence decision (Ultralytics Enterprise vs RF-DETR-only) is deferred and documented.
3. Edge inference + crop upload vs raw video upload: crops keep data under 1 GB/bus/month on Rs 100 IoT SIMs and avoid privacy issues (faces/plates never leave the vehicle beyond crops), at the cost of no post-hoc re-detection of missed potholes; Tier B vans upload full frames.
4. DA3METRIC-LARGE (newest, Apache, focal-aware, no published outdoor numbers) vs DA-V2-Metric (older, documented, fixed VKITTI scale): we lock scale with camera height either way so the model choice mainly affects relative geometry; both are swappable in `depth/models.py`.
5. OSRM/PostGIS nearest-way for the demo vs Valhalla Meili for production: avoids a long build for the hackathon, documented upgrade path.
6. Native PostgreSQL partitioning instead of TimescaleDB, Celery+Redis instead of Kafka: tens of thousands of observations/day do not justify heavier infra, and no Docker is available on the dev box.
7. Configurable priority weights (not a fixed IRC formula): IRC gives severity, not pothole-level priority; keeping weights in DB per agency keeps engineers in control and lets audit explain every score (priority_breakdown stored).
8. Auto-close by clean passes vs engineer sign-off: auto-close speeds throughput but risks closing on occluded/night passes; we require >= 3 clean passes AND a 10 % random engineer QC sample, with DLP reopen as the safety net.
9. eYantra masks are GPL-2: used for the prototype only; production masks come from pseudo-labelled RDD + self-collected Hyderabad data (CC BY-SA/own data).
10. Python 3.14 on the dev box: API runs on 3.14; ML workers may need a 3.12 venv if tensorrt/rfdetr wheels lag; kept isolated so neither blocks the other.
risks:
1. Depth accuracy unvalidated on Indian bus cameras: no published bus-mounted monocular ground-truth study; the DA3METRIC scaling convention is disputed. Mitigation: height-lock scale, synthetic bowl unit tests, cone/known-square check on day 1, inspector gauge + phone LiDAR ground truth before any billing use; always surface CIs and the measuring tier.
2. Water-filled and night/monsoon potholes under-measured or missed (20-30 % more misses at dusk). Mitigation: water_filled flag, IMU jolt corroboration, re-measure policy, citizen complaints merge.
3. Domain shift: RDD2022-India is Delhi/Haryana (flat, 720 px); Hyderabad has CC roads, white-topping, speed breakers, manholes. Mitigation: IDD negatives, pseudo-labelling of self-collected Hyderabad footage via RF-DETR teacher, engineer reject feedback loop into retraining.
4. GPS noise (5-15 m in Ameerpet/Koti canyons) and parallel/multi-lane roads break dedup. Mitigation: map matching, heading buckets, lane offset from camera geometry, >= 2 passes to confirm, Tier B precise GNSS.
5. Licensing: YOLO26 AGPL, eYantra GPL-2, UniDepth/Depth Pro NC (avoided). Mitigation: Segmenter abstraction with Apache RF-DETR path; licences.md.
6. Thermal/power on buses (phones throttle above 45 C, dev-kit Jetson rated to 35 C). Mitigation: shaded mounts, industrial carriers, throttle guard, depot Wi-Fi uploads.
7. Governance: ward boundaries changed in 2026 and are litigated; four road owners; CRMP DLP clauses "never invoked". Mitigation: pluggable admin units, jurisdiction queue, DLP events are evidence packages (before/after/re-detection) rather than automatic penalties; audit trail.
8. Data availability: BharatPotHole licence unverified, GHMC ward GeoJSON unofficial, IRC:82-2023 paywalled (we encode 2015 clauses, marked). Mitigation: all thresholds and rate tables configurable with citations.
9. Toolchain on Python 3.14 / CUDA 13.2: tensorrt and rfdetr wheels may lag; fallback ONNX Runtime CUDA EP and a 3.12 venv.
10. Adoption: citizen-only apps failed (RoadMetrics ~600 downloads); value depends on TSRTC fleet access and engineers actually working from the queue. Mitigation: operations-first UX in Telugu, daily indent per circle, measurement-book export that saves engineers paperwork, MoU with TGSRTC for 20-bus pilot across 3 depots.

name: GuntaDrishti (గుంత దృష్టి) — Edge-first bus-fleet pothole mapping with depth, volume and cold-mix quantities for Telangana
one_paragraph_pitch: GuntaDrishti turns the ~2,800 TGSRTC Greater-Hyderabad buses (each already carrying GPS/VTS and driving ~270 km/day on every arterial) into a free, continuous road-condition survey. A ₹10-15k Android phone or a Jetson/Pi edge box behind the windscreen runs an INT8/FP16 YOLO26n-seg pothole model on-device, keeps only frames with detections (crop + mask + 2 context frames + GPS/IMU), stores them in a local queue and uploads them over depot Wi-Fi or a ₹100/month IoT SIM. The server (the dev box today, a NIC/MeghRaj GPU VM tomorrow) runs the heavy models: a RF-DETR-Seg verifier to kill false positives (manholes, shadows, speed-breakers, puddles) and DA3METRIC-LARGE metric depth with camera-height scale correction, fits a RANSAC road plane, integrates depth-below-plane over the mask to get area, max depth, volume, then fuses 3-15 frames per pothole across bus approaches and passes. Potholes are map-matched to OSM ways, deduplicated with DBSCAN across the whole fleet, graded by IRC:82-2015 Cl. 7.5.3.4 (Small <25 mm, Medium 25-50 mm, Large >50 mm), prioritised by a configurable score (severity, bus-route exposure, schools/hospitals/bus stops nearby, age vs. GHMC 24-h charter, IMD rain), converted into IRC:116 / IRC:SP:100 cold-mix bag counts and rupee estimates, and routed as work orders to the correct road owner (GHMC / Cyberabad MC / Malkajgiri MC / R&B / NHAI / Cantonment) and CRMP contractor. The same buses verify the repair: N clean passes auto-close the work order, a re-opened pothole inside the defect-liability period flags the contractor. Everything (Telugu/Hindi/English PWA, MyCURE/WhatsApp intake, measurement-book export) is buildable now on the dev machine with public data (RDD2022-India, eYantra masks, BharatPotHole, TGSRTC GTFS, OSM Telangana).
architecture:
## 0. Design principles (edge-first)
1. Bandwidth is the scarce resource, not compute: the phone decides what is worth sending; the server never sees raw video. Budget: <1 GB/bus/month.
2. Server owns the truth and the hard maths (verifier model, metric depth, fusion). Edge models can be dumb and small; a bad edge FP costs 40 KB of upload, a bad edge FN costs a missed pothole that another bus will catch on the next pass (fleet redundancy is the recall mechanism).
3. Everything is idempotent and replayable: observations are immutable; potholes, severities, priorities are derived and can be recomputed when models improve.
4. Multi-tenant from day one (GHMC split into 3 corporations in 2026; R&B/NHAI/Cantonment own roads inside the city).

## 1. Components and data flow
```
[Bus edge unit] --(store&forward, JSON+WebP crops)--> [Ingest API] --> [MinIO/S3 + Postgres/PostGIS]
                                                              |
                                                              v  (Celery gpu queue)
                                          [Verifier RF-DETR-Seg] -> [Depth DA3METRIC + plane fit] -> [Per-frame measurement]
                                                              |
                                                              v  (Celery cpu queue)
                            [Map-match OSRM] -> [Track fusion across frames] -> [Fleet DBSCAN dedup] -> pothole entity
                                                              |
                                                              v
                         [Severity IRC:82] -> [Priority score] -> [Cold-mix quantity + cost] -> [Work order router]
                                                              |
                                                              v
                 [Field PWA (te/hi/en, offline)] <-> [Repair events] -> [Auto-verification from later passes] -> [Analytics / MB export]
                 [Citizen intake: MyCURE/WhatsApp/web form] ----------------^ (merges into same cluster logic)
```

## 2. Edge capture (bus / municipal vehicle)
**Hardware tiers (all Indian-priced):**
- Tier A (bus, pilot): Android phone ₹8-12k (Snapdragon 6-series or better, e.g. any 2024-26 Redmi/Realme with 4 GB RAM) in a shaded windscreen mount + 24 V -> 5 V isolated DC-DC with ignition-off delay (~₹600). Thermal: phones throttle at 45 °C; mount under sun-visor line, enable `PowerManager` thermal status callbacks to drop fps when `THERMAL_STATUS_SEVERE`.
- Tier A' (bus, production): Raspberry Pi 5 8 GB + Hailo-8L AI HAT (₹16-19k) or Jetson Orin Nano Super on an industrial carrier (RDP CARINA -20..70 °C, ~₹55-70k) + 2 MP global-shutter camera (IMX296/IMX462-GS module, ₹4-8k) + u-blox NEO-M8/M9 GNSS with NavIC where available (₹1.5-3k) + 4G Cat-1 modem. Same software, TensorRT/Hailo instead of LiteRT.
- Tier B (municipal inspection van / R&B jeep, 5-10 units for the city): Jetson Orin Nano + OAK-D Pro (₹30-35k) or ZED 2i (₹52-63k) stereo for ±10 % metric depth used for contractor billing disputes. Same server pipeline; stereo disparity replaces monocular depth map.
- Ground-truth kit (1 per circle): iPhone Pro LiDAR (volume error ~5 %) + straightedge + depth gauge (IRC manual method) for calibration/validation.

**Edge software (Android, Kotlin):**
- CameraX 1.5, 1280x720 @ 30 fps, exposure cap 8 ms (`CaptureRequest.SENSOR_EXPOSURE_TIME` via Camera2 interop) to keep blur ≤2.5 cm at 40 km/h; lock focus/zoom.
- Model: `yolo26n-seg` fine-tuned (see §4), exported `yolo export format=litert quantize=16 imgsz=640` -> LiteRT GPU delegate FP16 (~25-40 ms on Snapdragon 6-gen, 15-20 fps). INT8 (`quantize=8`) variant for Hailo/NNAPI-less chips; benchmark both. NMS-free head: no post-processing beyond confidence threshold 0.25 (deliberately low on edge; server verifier raises precision).
- Sampling by distance, not time: run inference only when `haversine(last_inferred_fix, now) >= 4 m` and speed >= 5 km/h (stationary at signals otherwise produces 100x duplicates). At 40 km/h this is ~2.8 inferences/s.
- Event packaging: on detection, write an `observation` record: `{device_id, trip_id, seq, ts_utc, lat, lon, accuracy_m, speed_mps, heading_deg, pitch/roll from rotation vector, imu_z_rms_1s, boxes[], masks (RLE, polygon in 640-space), conf[], model_ver, cam_calib_id}` + JPEG crop at 1.5x bbox (q85) + the full frame downscaled to 960x540 WebP q70 (needed server-side for depth/plane fit) + optional 2 context frames (t-0.5 s, t+0.5 s at 640 px) for multi-frame fusion. Typical event ~120-180 KB.
- Continuous light telemetry (1 Hz): `trip_fix` rows (lat, lon, acc, speed, heading, imu_z_rms) — ~60 B each, batched; this is what lets the server compute "clean passes" for repair verification and bus-route exposure.
- IMU jolt trigger: if `imu_z_rms_1s > threshold` and no camera detection, send a `jolt` observation with the current frame anyway (catches water-filled/night potholes; Boston/Harikrishnan precedent).
- Store-and-forward: Room/SQLite queue, WorkManager upload with constraints (unmetered preferred; metered allowed if `accuracy_m < 15` and queue > 50 MB or age > 6 h); resumable multipart to S3-compatible presigned URLs; exponential backoff; purge after server ACK. Depot Wi-Fi at the 29 Greater-Hyderabad depots drains queues nightly.
- OTA: model and threshold config fetched from `/api/edge/config` with ETag; model file signed (ed25519) and verified before load.
- Jetson/Pi variant: Python + GStreamer + TensorRT engine (`yolo export format=engine quantize=8 device=dla:0` on Orin) or Hailo `.hef`; same event schema; `gpsd` for GNSS; same uploader (Python `boto3` multipart).

## 3. Server stack (dev box today)
- API: FastAPI 0.162.x, uvicorn, pydantic 2; auth pyjwt + argon2-cffi; roles `citizen, driver_device, field_engineer, contractor, zonal_admin, super_admin`; tenant/zone scoping by dependency.
- DB: PostgreSQL 18 + PostGIS 3.6 (apt packages, no docker). SQLAlchemy 2.0.x (pin <2.1 to keep GeoAlchemy2 safe) + psycopg 3 + alembic. Native monthly partitioning on `observations` and `trip_fixes`.
- Storage: MinIO single binary via `boto3` (S3 API; portable to MeghRaj).
- Queue: Redis 8 + Celery 5.7: queues `gpu` (verifier+depth, `--pool=solo`, prefetch 1, batch 16 frames), `cpu` (map-match, fusion, dedup, scoring), `notify`.
- Map matching: OSRM (binary + Geofabrik `india/southern-zone` clipped to Telangana) `/match` for hackathon; Valhalla Meili later.
- ML: torch 2.12+ cu130 wheels, ultralytics 8.4.211, rfdetr, Depth-Anything-3 (`pip install -e` from ByteDance-Seed repo), open3d or pure numpy RANSAC, opencv-headless, shapely, pyproj, h3, scikit-learn.
- Python: use a **3.12 venv** for the ML services (`uv venv -p 3.12`) because tensorrt/rfdetr/onnxruntime-gpu may lag on 3.14; the API can run on 3.14 or the same 3.12 venv — simplest: one 3.12 venv for everything.
- Frontend: React 19 + Vite 8 + MapLibre GL 6 + TanStack Query + zustand + i18next (te/hi/en, Noto Sans Telugu/Devanagari) + vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox background sync, Dexie offline queue). Tiles: self-hosted PMTiles of Telangana (Protomaps) from MinIO; pothole vector tiles via `ST_AsMVT`.

## 4. Models (exact ids, all downloadable now)
**Detection/segmentation edge model:** `yolo26n-seg.pt` and `yolo26s-seg.pt` from `Ultralytics/YOLO26` (HF) / GitHub releases. Training data (built by `data/build_dataset.py`):
- RDD2022 India zip (boxes, D40 pothole 3,187 + crack classes; merge D00/D10/D20 -> `crack`). Boxes converted to pseudo-masks via SAM2 (`facebook/sam2.1-hiera-small`) prompted with the box; manually QC a sample.
- eYantra "Semantic Segmentation Dataset of Indian Roads" (Kaggle `eyantraiit/semantic-segmentation-datasets-of-indian-roads`) — the only true Indian pothole masks; also gives `shallow` (water-filled/depression) class.
- BharatPotHole (Kaggle `surbhisaswatimohanty/bharatpothole`) boxes -> SAM2 masks (verify licence; fall back to RDD-only if unusable).
- Roboflow `vnr-project/pothole-segmentation-8esmn` (possibly Hyderabad) polygon masks.
- Negatives: manhole covers, speed-breakers, shadows, wet patches, road paint — harvested from IDD (IIIT-H Hyderabad imagery, no damage labels, used as pure negatives) and from RDD-India frames without D40.
- Classes: `pothole, water_filled_pothole, crack, manhole, speed_breaker` (last two exist only to absorb FPs; dropped from reporting).
- Train: `yolo segment train model=yolo26s-seg.pt data=indian_potholes.yaml imgsz=640 epochs=100 batch=32 mosaic=1.0 hsv_v=0.5 degrees=3 fliplr=0.5` (+ monsoon augmentations: rain streaks, glare, low-light via albumentations). Export `litert` FP16/INT8, `onnx`, `engine`.
- Warm start option: `mfranzon/pothole-yolo26` or `TamAko783/YOLO26n_RDD_FRDC_Distilled_v2` weights.

**Server verifier/teacher:** RF-DETR-Seg-Small (`pip install rfdetr`, Apache 2.0), fine-tuned on the same set; a detection survives only if verifier IoU ≥ 0.4 with class pothole/water_filled; it also refines the mask. Serves as pseudo-labeller for Hyderabad self-collected frames (active-learning loop: low-agreement frames go to a CVAT/Label Studio queue).

**Depth:** `depth-anything/DA3METRIC-LARGE` (Apache 2.0) with calibrated `fx` passed in; fallback `depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Metric-VKITTI-Base` (Apache per card). Edge/ONNX later option: `onnx-community/metric3d-vit-small` (BSD). Stereo Tier B: SGBM/ZED SDK disparity -> depth. All go through the same `geometry/plane_fit.py` and `geometry/volume.py`.

## 5. Depth, area and volume method — see depth_method field (summary: metric depth -> point cloud -> RANSAC road plane on ring region -> scale by known camera height -> depth-below-plane integrated over mask -> multi-frame Kalman fusion).

## 6. Geolocation, fusion and fleet dedup
1. Map-match each trip's fixes with OSRM `/match` -> every observation gets `way_id`, `dir_bucket` (heading ±45°), `chainage_m` along the way, `lateral_offset_m` (from mask centroid x via the plane homography: distance from camera axis), and corrected lat/lon snapped onto the way.
2. Within-trip track fusion: observations of the same pothole over consecutive frames (BoT-SORT ids from the edge, or server re-association by predicted ground position ± 1.5 m) are merged by a 1-D Kalman per metric (depth_max, area, volume) with measurement variance ∝ Z² (closer = trusted). Output one `track_measurement`.
3. Fleet dedup: within `(way_id, dir_bucket)` rolling 30-day window, DBSCAN (`metric='haversine'`, eps = 6 m, min_samples = 1) on snapped positions, then split clusters whose lateral offsets differ > 1.5 m (adjacent lanes). Cluster -> `pothole` entity, state machine: `candidate` (1 pass) -> `confirmed` (≥2 passes from ≥2 distinct trips, or 1 pass + citizen complaint) -> `work_ordered` -> `repaired_reported` -> `verified_closed` (≥3 subsequent passes with camera active through the cell and no detection, within 14 days) -> `reopened` if re-detected (DLP breach flag if inside warranty).
4. Pothole aggregates: median of track measurements (robust), `depth_class` from the 75th percentile of depth_max across tracks, `volume_l`, `area_m2`, `water_filled` share, first/last seen, pass counts (seen/total).

## 7. Severity (IRC:82-2015 Cl. 7.5.3.4) and prioritisation
- `severity = Large` if depth > 50 mm or width > 500 mm; `Medium` if 25-50 mm or width ≈ 200-500 mm; `Small` otherwise. Water-filled with unknown depth: severity from width + IMU jolt magnitude, flagged `depth_unknown`.
- Stretch-level rating per IRC:82 Table 5.3 (urban): pothole area % of carriageway per 100 m segment: >0.5 % Poor, 0-0.5 % Fair, nil Good — computed from summed `area_m2` / (segment length × lanes × 3.5 m).
- Priority score (0-100, weights editable per tenant in `priority_config`):
  `P = 100·(0.30·S + 0.25·E + 0.20·V + 0.15·T + 0.10·M)`
  - S: Large 1.0 / Medium 0.6 / Small 0.3; +0.2 if in wheel path (|lateral_offset − lane_centre| < 1.2 m) or ≤ 30 m from a junction; +0.1 if water-filled; clip to 1.
  - E (exposure): `0.5·road_class` (OSM primary/trunk 1.0, secondary 0.7, tertiary 0.5, residential 0.3) + `0.5·min(1, bus_passes_per_day/50)` from TGSRTC GTFS route frequency × trip telemetry.
  - V (vulnerability): 1 − exp(−n/3) where n = schools + hospitals + bus stops (GTFS stops.txt) + metro stations within 200 m (Overpass/GHMC amenities dataset); +0.2 if no street lighting tag.
  - T (age/SLA): `min(1, days_open / sla_days)`; sla_days = 1 (arterial, monsoon; GHMC Citizen Charter 24 h), 3 (others, monsoon), 7 (dry season); breach => +0.3.
  - M (monsoon): 1.0 base, scaled by IMD district rainfall last 72 h (open IMD API or manual flag): >25 mm -> 1.3, >65 mm -> 1.5; waterlogging hotspot (GHMC list) -> ×1.2.
- Work-order batching: greedy cluster of top-P potholes within 500 m on the same road-owner, so one crew/jet-patcher trip handles 5-20 holes; MB export per batch.

## 8. Repair planning module (cold-mix, IRC:116 / IRC:SP:100)
- Square-cut repair area: `A_cut = (L + 2·m) × (W + 2·m)`, m = 0.10-0.15 m margin (IRC:82 Cl. 11.4 "cut adjoining deteriorated portion").
- Design depth: `d_design = max(d_p95, 0.050)` m (minimum 50 mm patch per IRC:116 top-layer rule); if `d_design > 0.075`: lower layer CRM/angular aggregate `d_design − 0.050` and 50 mm patching mix on top; layers ≤ 75 mm.
- Volume for material: `V_mix = A_cut × min(d_design, 0.075-layer logic)`, plus true cavity volume `V_cavity` from the integral (reported separately — the 2-4× cuboid over-estimate from the LiDAR-TIN study is the saving we show).
- Mass: `M = V_mix × 2200 kg/m³ × (1 + wastage 0.12)`; bags = `ceil(M / bag_kg)` with bag_kg 25 (trade) or 50 (IRC:116).
- Tack/prime: `0.3 kg/m² × A_cut` SS-1/CSS-1 emulsion.
- Cost: `bags × ₹350 + emulsion_kg × ₹45 + labour (2.5 man-h × ₹100/h) + sand ₹30`; all unit rates in `material_rates` table per tenant (defaults from IndiaMART/HINCOL evidence). Example 0.5×0.4 m × 60 mm -> 0.7×0.6×0.06 = 0.0252 m³ -> 62 kg -> 3 × 25 kg bags -> ≈ ₹1,050 material, ≈ ₹1,600 all-in vs GHMC's reported ₹7,396.
- Method recommendation: `cold_mix_bags` default; `jet_patcher` if ≥ 8 confirmed Large potholes within 300 m; `infrared` if water-filled and arterial; `hot_mix` only if a plant is within 10 km and dry season (Chudi Bazar cold-arrival issue). Stored as `material_spec` reference: `IRC:116-2014` (cut-back readymade) or `IRC:SP:100-2014` (emulsion).
- Weather gate: suppress scheduling when IMD forecast rain > 10 mm in next 6 h unless material is emulsion patching mix (IRC:SP:100 allows damp holes; "excess water shall be removed").

## 9. Work orders, repair and verification loop
- Road-owner router: `road_owner` polygon/line layer (GHMC/Cyberabad MC/Malkajgiri MC zones; R&B and NHAI ways tagged by OSM `ref`/`operator` + manual overrides; Cantonment polygon). `contractor_package` layer (CRMP Phase 1/2 package polygons, DLP end dates). Pothole -> owner -> package -> contractor.
- Work order fields: pothole ids, batch, priority, SLA due, material_spec, bags, est cost, assigned crew/contractor, status.
- Field PWA (offline): crew sees route-ordered list, before/after photos (geo+time-stamped, client-resized 1280 px, queued in IndexedDB), batch number of cold-mix bags used, actual bags consumed (vs estimate — feeds model recalibration and contractor audit).
- Verification: automatic from bus passes (state machine above) + manual QC sample 10 % by field engineer + citizen re-report. Contractor invoice allowed only against `verified_closed`. Reopen within DLP (5-yr CRMP package or 6-month patch warranty) -> `dlp_breach` event, zero-pay rework, debit note draft.
- Citizen intake: web form + WhatsApp bot stub (Twilio/Meta Cloud API) + MyCURE CSV import; each creates an `observation` with `source='citizen'` that joins the same DBSCAN step.
- Notifications: SMS/WhatsApp to engineer on SLA breach; weekly PDF per circle.

## 10. Analytics dashboard
MapLibre map with clustered potholes coloured by severity/priority, filters by zone/circle/ward (pluggable ward GeoJSON layer), road-owner, contractor; KPIs: open/confirmed/verified counts, median repair days, SLA compliance, bags consumed vs estimated, ₹ saved vs cuboid estimate, recurrence rate per contractor, km surveyed per day by fleet, stretch ratings (IRC Table 5.3). Public transparency page per ward. Exports: GeoJSON (for GHMC ArcGIS Field Maps), CSV measurement book, eMARG-style inspection-payment linkage report.

## 11. APIs (FastAPI, `/api/v1`)
- Edge: `POST /edge/register` (device, camera calib), `GET /edge/config` (ETag), `POST /edge/presign` (S3 multipart), `POST /edge/observations` (batch JSON, idempotent by `device_id+seq`), `POST /edge/fixes` (1 Hz telemetry batch).

- Ops: `POST /workorders/batch`, `PATCH /workorders/{id}`, `POST /workorders/{id}/repair-events` (multipart photos), `GET /contractors/{id}/scorecard`, `GET /export/mb.csv`, `GET /priority-config`, `PUT /priority-config` (admin).
- Admin: `GET /models`, `POST /models/publish` (signed), `GET /fleet/coverage` (km surveyed per way per day).

depth_method:
Goal: per pothole, metric max depth (mm), area (m²), volume (L), length/width (m) from a single forward-facing camera at 5-15 m range, robust enough to bin IRC:82 severity (25/50 mm) and estimate cold-mix mass to ±20-30 %; Tier B stereo for billing-grade numbers.

Per frame (server, `ml/depth/`):
1. Inputs: full frame (960x540 WebP from edge), pothole mask M from RF-DETR-Seg (refined), calib (fx, fy, cx, cy, distortion, mounting height h_true, nominal pitch). Undistort frame and mask.
2. Metric depth map Z = DA3METRIC-LARGE(frame, focal_px = fx_scaled) (`metric_depth = fx * net_out / 300` per HF card — validated once against a tape-measured hole in `calibrate.py` and corrected by the scale step anyway). Fallback DA-V2-Metric-VKITTI-Base. Tier B: Z from stereo disparity, same below.
3. Back-project to camera-frame points P = Z·K⁻¹[u,v,1]ᵀ.
4. Road plane: take ring region R = dilate(M, 2.5×bbox) \ dilate(M, 1.15×bbox), intersected with a road prior (lower 60 % of image, not sky/vehicle via DA3 sky mask or a cheap road-seg head). RANSAC plane n·p + d = 0 on R (threshold 15 mm, 500 iters, numpy), refit by least squares on inliers; reject frame if inlier ratio < 0.6 or plane RMSE > 25 mm (quality flag). Camera height estimate ĥ = |d| / ||n||.
5. Scale correction: s = h_true / ĥ (clipped to [0.6, 1.6], else frame rejected). Multiply all Z by s. This removes most monocular absolute-scale error (the Gamma-from-Mono insight) and makes the result tied to a tape-measured number, not to the model's training camera. Online drift check: rolling median of ĥ per trip; alert if drift > 5 %.
6. Per pixel in M: signed distance below plane δ_i = −(n·p_i + d)/||n|| (positive = cavity). Clamp δ ≥ 0; depth_max = 98th percentile of δ (robust to spikes), depth_p95, depth_mean.
7. Footprint area of pixel i on the plane: a_i = (Z_i/fx)·(Z_i/fy) / cosθ where θ is the angle between the camera ray and the plane normal (equivalently IPM). area = Σ a_i over M; volume = Σ δ_i·a_i. Length/width from the oriented bounding rectangle of the mask projected on the plane (metres).
8. Water-filled test: RGB class `water_filled_pothole` OR (depth_max < 8 mm and mask area > 0.05 m² and specular/low-texture score high) -> `water_filled = true, depth = unknown`; severity then from width + IMU jolt; re-measure after rain.
9. Distance gating: measurements accepted only for 3 m ≤ Z_centroid ≤ 15 m; measurement variance σ²_depth ∝ Z², σ²_vol ∝ Z⁴ (used by fusion).

Per track (bus approaching, 3-15 frames): 1-D Kalman per metric with the above variances, constant state; final estimate dominated by the last 3-6 m before passing. Per pothole (fleet): median over tracks; depth_class from p75 of track depth_max; confidence from number of tracks and plane-quality flags.

Material quantity from these (domain/coldmix.py): A_cut = (L+0.25)(W+0.25); d_design = max(d_p95, 50 mm); layers ≤ 75 mm, CRM below 50 mm top; mass = A_cut·d_design·2200·1.12; bags = ceil(mass/25).

Calibration SOP (docs/CALIBRATION_SOP.md): intrinsics once per camera model (9×6 checkerboard, 30 mm, 20 poses, reproj < 0.3 px); per bus at depot 10 min: tape camera height, 4 cones at 3/5/8/12 m -> solvePnP pitch/roll/yaw; 1 m painted square at 5 m must reconstruct within 5 %; online lane-width prior (3.5 m on marked arterials) and vanishing point for drift.

Validation plan: 50-100 potholes measured by inspector (straightedge + depth gauge) and iPhone LiDAR; report depth MAE and volume MAPE per distance bin and per tier; expected monocular single-frame ±10-25 mm depth / ±20-40 % volume, fused ±5-15 mm / ±15-25 %; stereo Tier B ~±12 % depth. The demo shows this table on real self-shot Hyderabad potholes plus RDD frames.
key_tradeoffs:
1. Monocular depth on buses vs stereo everywhere: monocular is ₹10-15k per bus and good enough for IRC severity bins and bulk material estimates; stereo (₹30-60k + Jetson) is reserved for 5-10 inspection vans where numbers feed contractor billing. The same geometry code serves both, so the choice is per-vehicle, not architectural.
2. Edge detection + server depth vs all-on-edge: depth models (0.35B params) are impractical on phones and need full frames; running only YOLO26n-seg on-edge keeps upload <1 GB/bus/month and lets depth improve server-side without touching 2,800 devices.
3. Low edge threshold + server verifier vs high edge precision: we accept more uploads (cheap) to protect recall; RF-DETR verifier and ≥2-pass confirmation restore precision. Fleet redundancy, not per-frame accuracy, is the quality lever.
4. YOLO26 (AGPL, fastest NMS-free edge export) vs RF-DETR (Apache) everywhere: use YOLO26 for the hackathon edge model and flag the Ultralytics Enterprise licence for government procurement; RF-DETR-Seg-Nano is the licence-clean swap for edge if needed (slightly slower on LiteRT).
5. Android phone vs Jetson/Pi on buses: phones are cheapest and fastest to pilot but throttle above 45 °C and are theft-prone; Pi 5 + Hailo in a ventilated box is the production path. Same event schema makes both interchangeable.
6. DBSCAN per (way_id, direction) vs plain spatial clustering: more plumbing (OSRM) but it is the only way to avoid merging potholes on opposite carriageways/flyovers and to compute chainage for R&B.
7. Square-cut design volume vs integrated cavity volume: bags are computed from the IRC square-cut rule (what crews must actually place), while the integrated volume is reported to show the saving vs cuboid L×W×D estimates (2-4× overestimation in literature); both are stored.
8. Postgres partitioning vs TimescaleDB: native partitions + BRIN cover tens of thousands of observations/day with zero extra ops; revisit only if 1 Hz telemetry for 10k buses is retained long-term.
9. Python 3.12 venv vs the box's 3.14: 3.12 avoids unresolved wheels (tensorrt, rfdetr, onnxruntime-gpu) at the cost of not using the system interpreter.
10. Configurable weights (priority, rates, SLA) vs hard-coded IRC values: IRC severity is fixed in code (standard), everything policy-like lives in DB per tenant because GHMC/Cyberabad/Malkajgiri/R&B will disagree.
risks:
1. Monocular absolute accuracy unproven on buses (no published GT study): mitigated by camera-height scale correction, multi-frame fusion, distance gating and a mandatory 50-100 pothole validation set; present results as severity-class accuracy, not mm precision. Stereo Tier B as fallback for billing.
2. Water-filled potholes during monsoon (the season that matters): depth models see a flat surface. Handled by explicit water class, depth_unknown flag, width + IMU jolt severity, re-measure after rain; honestly stated in the demo.
3. Domain shift: RDD2022 is Delhi/Haryana, eYantra is small, BharatPotHole licence unverified; Hyderabad has no public labels. Mitigated by IDD negatives, pseudo-labelling with RF-DETR teacher, active-learning queue, and a plan to label 1-2k Hyderabad frames in week 1 of the pilot.
4. False positives from manholes, speed-breakers, shadows, patch scars (the top Indian FP sources): explicit negative classes, verifier model, ≥2-pass confirmation; measure FP rate on held-out IDD frames.
5. GPS 5-15 m error in Ameerpet/Koti canyons and multi-lane ambiguity: map matching + lateral offset from the camera geometry + direction bucket; accept that parallel service roads may still merge and expose a manual split tool.
6. Edge hardware in Telangana heat (45 °C+ in bus cabins): phone throttling/shutdown; mitigation = thermal callbacks, shaded mounts, Pi/Jetson industrial carriers for production.
7. Licensing: YOLO26 AGPL (needs Enterprise licence for govt production), eYantra GPL-2.0 (prototype only), Depth Pro/UniDepth NC (avoided), IRC PDFs (quote clauses, do not redistribute 2023 editions).
8. Toolchain uncertainty: torch cu130 on Python 3.14, tensorrt/rfdetr wheels, DA3 focal scaling convention; all isolated behind backend interfaces and a 3.12 venv; ONNX Runtime CUDA as TensorRT fallback.
9. Institutional: four road owners, GHMC trifurcation, contested ward boundaries, CRMP DLP clauses not public; schema keeps owner/package/ward layers as replaceable GeoJSON and SLAs configurable. RoadMetrics pilot outcome unknown — do not over-promise; the verification loop and material quantities are the differentiators.
10. TGSRTC cooperation and power/connectivity on buses: pilot on 20-50 buses from 2-3 depots with depot Wi-Fi; nothing in the design depends on live connectivity.
11. Privacy: faces/number plates in crops; apply on-server blurring before any public exposure and retain full frames only 90 days.

2. Create DB `guntadrishti`, enable postgis; create MinIO buckets `frames`, `crops`, `tiles`, `models`.

Phase 1 — Data (day 1)
3. `data/download.py`: RDD2022_India.zip (S3), eYantra via kaggle CLI, BharatPotHole (check licence; skip if unusable), Roboflow vnr-project set, IDD sample (register), TGSRTC GTFS mdb-3361, Geofabrik southern-zone PBF, Telangana boundaries GeoJSON, GHMC amenities CSV.

7. `ml/depth/backends.py` + `plane_fit.py` + `volume.py` + `fusion.py` + unit tests on synthetic planes with known cavities (exact analytic volumes) and on 5-10 photos of real Hyderabad potholes measured with a tape (collect on day 2).

Phase 3 — Domain logic (day 2, pure Python, TDD)
8. `server/domain/irc.py` (severity, Table 5.3 rating, layering), `coldmix.py`, `priority.py`, `router.py` with pytest covering the worked example (0.5×0.4×60 mm -> 3 bags).

Phase 4 — Server (days 2-4)

Integration test: feed 3 synthetic trips over the same pothole, assert one `confirmed` pothole, then 3 clean passes -> `verified_closed`.

Phase 6 — Edge (days 3-5)

13. `edge/android/`: Kotlin app — CameraX capture, LiteRT GPU inference with exported yolo26n-seg, distance sampler, Room queue, WorkManager uploader with presigned multipart, OTA config, thermal handling. Test on one phone against the dev box over Wi-Fi.

name: RoadFix (గుంత = pothole) — Measurement-first pothole mapping, volumetric cold-mix planning and verified repair for Telangana
one_paragraph_pitch: RoadFix turns every TGSRTC bus and GHMC/R&B vehicle into a calibrated road-measuring instrument. A ₹10–40k camera kit (Android phone or Jetson Orin Nano + global-shutter cam) runs a YOLO26-seg pothole/manhole/speed-breaker segmenter on-vehicle and uploads only crops, masks, GPS and IMU jolts (<1 GB/bus/month). On the server, a metric monocular depth model (Depth Anything 3 METRIC-LARGE, Apache-2.0, fed the calibrated focal length) plus a RANSAC road-plane fit rescaled by the tape-measured camera height give per-pixel depth below the road surface, integrated over the mask into max depth, area and volume with an explicit uncertainty band, fused over 5–15 frames as the vehicle approaches, and corroborated by the IMU jolt when the wheel hits it. Water-filled holes are detected and flagged rather than silently under-measured. Depth maps straight onto IRC:82-2015 cl. 7.5.3.4 severity (Small ≤25 mm/200 mm, Medium 25–50 mm/500 mm, Large >50 mm/>500 mm), and volume (with IRC:82/IRC:116 square-cut margin, ≥50 mm minimum and 75 mm layering rules) becomes exact bags of IRC:116 / IRC:SP:100 cold mix, tack-coat emulsion and cost — the Measurement Book entry for the work order. Detections are map-matched to OSM ways, deduplicated across passes (DBSCAN per way+direction), confirmed only on ≥2 independent passes, prioritised by a configurable IRC-aligned score (severity, exposure incl. bus-route pass-counts, vulnerability from GTFS stops/schools/hospitals, age vs GHMC 24-h charter, IMD rain), routed to the owning agency (GHMC/Cyberabad MC/Malkajgiri MC/R&B/NHAI/Cantonment) and contractor package (CRMP), and auto-verified closed when N later bus passes see a flat road — with recurrence inside the defect-liability period flagged as contractor-liable. Everything runs today on the dev box with public Indian data (RDD2022-India D40, eYantra Indian road masks, BharatPotHole) and a Telugu/Hindi/English offline-first PWA.
architecture:
## 0. Guiding decisions (analysis & debate summary)
- Measurement-first: the hard, differentiating requirement is credible depth → volume → material. Everything else (dedup, priority, work orders) is designed around a `measurement` record that carries a value AND an uncertainty AND a method tag (mono / mono+imu / stereo / manual-gauge / phone-lidar), so cheaper bus data and dearer inspection-van data live in one schema and the billing path can require a minimum quality.
- Edge does detection only; depth runs server-side (GPU). Reason: metric depth models are 0.35 B params; a ₹12k phone cannot run them, a Jetson can but a central GPU re-runs with newer models over archived crops, and bus bandwidth is the constraint, not server GPU. Jetson tier runs depth locally only for the stereo inspection van.
- Monocular + plane-fit + height rescale is the primary depth method (Tier A, buses); stereo (OAK-D Pro / ZED 2i) is Tier B on municipal vans for billing-grade numbers; iPhone-LiDAR + straightedge/depth-gauge is the ground-truth tier for calibration certificates. One geometry library serves all three.
- Python 3.11 venv already present at /home/coral/Desktop/Telangana pathole detection/.venv (torch 2.11.0+cu128, CUDA works on RTX 5080 sm_120). Use it; do NOT fight Python 3.14 wheel gaps (rfdetr, onnxruntime-gpu, tensorrt). Node 22 for the frontend.
- Licences for govt deployment: YOLO26 is AGPL (prototype OK; flag Ultralytics Enterprise licence or swap to RF-DETR-Seg Apache for production); DA3METRIC-LARGE Apache; Metric3D v2 BSD fallback; avoid UniDepth/Depth Pro (NC). PostGIS/MapLibre/FastAPI all permissive.

## 1. Components and data flow
```
[Edge kit on bus/van]  --4G/depot Wi-Fi-->  [Ingest API]  -->  [Redis queue]  -->  [GPU worker: seg verify + depth + geometry]
   YOLO26n-seg LiteRT/TensorRT                FastAPI            Celery/arq              -> measurement rows
   GPS+IMU logger, distance-triggered                                                     |
   store-and-forward SQLite                                                               v
                                                                 [Geo worker: map-match (OSRM) + DBSCAN dedup + pass counting]
                                                                                           |
[Citizen WhatsApp/MyCURE intake] ---> same cluster logic <------------------------------------+
                                                                                           v
                                              [Priority engine] -> [Work-order & material planner] -> [Field PWA (te/hi/en), contractor portal]
                                                                                           |
                                              [Verification: clean-pass counter + photo QC] <-- later bus passes
                                                                                           v
                                              [Dashboard: MapLibre + PostGIS MVT, analytics, open-data export]
```

### 1.1 Edge capture (`edge/`)
- Hardware Tier A (bus, ~2,800 Greater Hyderabad buses): Android phone ₹8–12k (CameraX 1.5, LiteRT GPU FP16 YOLO26n-seg at 640 px, 10–20 fps) in a shaded, fan-cooled windshield mount powered by 24→5 V isolated DC-DC; or Jetson Orin Nano (industrial carrier, -10..60 °C) + 2 MP global-shutter camera (IMX296) at ≤8 ms exposure, pitch 15–25° down. Dev demo substitutes a Python "virtual bus" (`edge/sim/`) that replays dashcam video + GPX.
- Sampling: distance-triggered keyframe every ≥4 m (skip <5 km/h), GNSS 1 Hz (record `accuracy_m`, NavIC L5 where available), IMU 100 Hz z-accel/gyro, synced by monotonic clock (iWatchRoad's OCR-timestamp bug avoided by design).
- On-device output per detection: 2 context frames (1280 px JPEG q=80) + mask polygon + bbox + conf + GPS/heading/speed + IMU window (±1 s) + device/calibration id. Store-and-forward SQLite queue; upload via resumable multipart (tus) over depot Wi-Fi or 4G. Payload ≈ 150 KB/detection.
- Negative classes trained in: `manhole`, `speed_breaker`, `shadow_patch`, `wet_patch`, `utility_cut` (top Indian FP sources). Classes: `pothole`, `pothole_water`, `alligator_crack`, `crack`, `manhole`, `speed_breaker`, `utility_cut`.

### 1.2 Detection + segmentation (`ml/`)
- Edge model: `yolo26n-seg` / `yolo26s-seg` (ultralytics 8.4.211, base weights from `Ultralytics/YOLO26` HF). Train imgsz 640 (bus kit) and 1024 (server verifier) on:
  - RDD2022 India (7,706 train imgs, D40 pothole 3,187 boxes) — boxes converted to masks with SAM2 (`facebook/sam2.1-hiera-large`) box prompts, then human-spot-checked in Label Studio.
  - eYantra "Semantic Segmentation Dataset of Indian Roads" (Kaggle `eyantraiit/semantic-segmentation-datasets-of-indian-roads`, 3,227 imgs, true pothole masks, GPL-2 — prototype only).
  - BharatPotHole (Kaggle `surbhisaswatimohanty/bharatpothole`, 7k dashcam frames, monsoon season) — boxes → SAM2 masks.
  - Roboflow `vnr-project/pothole-segmentation-8esmn` (possibly Hyderabad) + `utm-cuu2y/potholes-segmentation` for extra masks; `chitholian/annotated-potholes-dataset` negatives/pos.
  - IDD (IIIT-H, Hyderabad scenes) as pothole-free hard negatives + road-mask pretraining.
  - Bootstrap checkpoint for day-1 demo: `mfranzon/pothole-yolo26` (YOLO26m) via `hf_hub_download`.
- Server verifier/teacher: RF-DETR-Seg-Small (`pip install rfdetr`, Apache) fine-tuned on same data; disagreements between edge and verifier go to a review queue; verifier pseudo-labels self-collected Hyderabad footage (active learning loop).
- Augmentations for India: monsoon rain streaks, wet-asphalt specular, dusk/low-light, motion blur ≤2.5 cm, dust haze, mixed CC/BT surfaces.
- Exports: `yolo export format=litert quantize=16` (Android), `format=engine quantize=16` on Jetson (TRT 10.x), `format=onnx` for server ORT-CUDA.

### 1.3 Depth → volume (`measure/`) — see depth_method; here the module boundaries
- `measure/calib.py`: intrinsics (OpenCV checkerboard), extrinsics (PnP from depot cones), per-device JSON cert with reprojection error, fx, h, pitch, roll, scale-check history.
- `measure/depth_backends/`: `da3_metric.py` (primary), `da2_metric_vkitti.py`, `metric3d_v2.py` (ONNX, edge-capable), `stereo_oakd.py`, `stereo_sgbm.py` (two Pi GS cams). Common interface `predict(img, fx) -> depth_m (H,W), conf (H,W)`.
- `measure/plane.py`: road-plane RANSAC (open3d), camera-height rescale, per-pixel footprint, IPM.
- `measure/pothole_geom.py`: mask → depth profile, area, volume, uncertainty, water flag.
- `measure/fuse.py`: BoT-SORT track + Kalman fusion over frames, distance-weighted.
- `measure/imu.py`: jolt-to-depth corroboration (Harikrishnan-Gopi 1-DoF model, per-vehicle gain).
- `measure/truth.py`: ingest inspector straightedge+gauge and iPhone LiDAR (.ply) measurements; compute MAE/MAPE per distance bin; produce calibration certificate.

### 1.4 Geolocation & dedup (`geo/`)
- Map-match each trip trace with OSRM `/match` (Geofabrik southern-zone PBF clipped to Telangana; Valhalla Meili later). Each detection gets `way_id`, `direction_bucket` (heading ±45°), `chainage_m` (ST_LineLocatePoint), `lane_offset_m` (from mask x-centroid via IPM), `h3_r12`.
- Position refinement: pothole ground point = camera GPS + IPM range/bearing (not the camera position), reducing 8–15 m GNSS lag error.
- DBSCAN (`eps`=8 m haversine, `min_samples`=2) inside (`way_id`,`direction_bucket`) over rolling 30 days → `pothole` entity; detections → `observations`. Status: `candidate` (1 pass) → `confirmed` (≥2 passes from ≥2 trips or 1 pass + citizen report) → `work_ordered` → `repaired_reported` → `verified_closed` (≥3 clean passes within 14 days) → `reopened` (re-detect within DLP).
- Per-way pass counter from all buses (free exposure metric) stored hourly in `way_passes`.

### 1.5 Prioritisation (`priority/`)
Score 0–100, weights in `priority_config` table per ULB:
`P = 100·(0.30·S + 0.25·E + 0.20·V + 0.15·T + 0.10·M)`
- S severity: Large (depth_p95 ≥50 mm or width ≥500 mm) = 1.0; Medium = 0.6; Small = 0.3; +0.2 if in wheel path (|lane_offset| < 1.2 m) or ≤30 m from junction; water_filled with unknown depth → S = 0.6 min, 0.8 if area ≥0.3 m².
- E exposure: OSM class weight (trunk/primary 1.0, secondary 0.8, tertiary 0.6, residential 0.4) × min(1, bus_passes_per_day/50) blended 50/50; TSRTC GTFS route overlap bonus.
- V vulnerability: POIs within 200 m (school/hospital 1.0, bus stop/metro 0.7, market 0.5, max-pooled), night-unlit flag +0.2.
- T age: min(1, days_open/14) + 0.3 if GHMC 24-h charter breached.
- M monsoon: IMD district 72-h rain (open IMD API/nowcast) scaled 0–1, ×1.5 if waterlogging hotspot list.
Also stretch-level IRC:82 Table 5.3 rating: pothole % area of carriageway per 100 m chainage bin → Good/Fair/Poor.

### 1.6 Repair planning & material module (`repair/`)
Inputs: measurement (A_mask, d_mean, d_p95, d_max, bbox L×W on plane), surface type (BT/CC from GHMC layer or classifier), water flag.
- Square-cut area: `A_cut = (L + 2·m)·(W + 2·m)`, m = 100–150 mm (IRC:82 cl. 11.4 cutting of deteriorated edges); for clustered potholes within 0.5 m, merge into one cut.
- Design depth: `d_design = max(d_p95, 50 mm)` (IRC:116 cl. 5.2: ≥50 mm patching mix). If d_design > 75 mm: layers per IRC:82 Sec 10 / IRC:SP:100 cl. 9.7 — bottom `d_design − 50 mm` Crusher Run Macadam (or more cold-mix layers ≤75 mm each) + 50 mm top patching mix.
- Volume: `V_patch = A_cut · min(d_design, 50 mm if layered else d_design)`, `V_crm = A_cut · max(0, d_design − 50 mm)`; integrated real volume V_int from measurement also stored (cuboid over-estimates 2–4× per LiDAR TIN study — we bill by integrated-plus-cut, not L×W×D).
- Mass: `M_mix = V_patch · 2200 kg/m³ · (1 + 0.12 wastage)`; `bags = ceil(M_mix / bag_kg)` (25 kg trade bags default; 50 kg per IRC:116); tack/prime emulsion `0.3 kg/m² · A_cut` (SS-1/CSS-1); sand blotting `1 kg/m²`.
- Cost (all unit rates in `rate_card` table, editable): bags × ₹350 + emulsion × ₹45/kg + CRM × ₹1,800/m³ + labour 2.5 man-h × ₹100 + transport share; compare against GHMC baseline ₹7,396/pothole (Deccan Chronicle 2021) on the dashboard.
- Method selector: cold-mix hand patch (default, all weather, hole need not be dry — IRC:82 Appendix); jet patcher if ≥20 potholes within 500 m or A_cut < 0.3 m² (₹1,942/m² BBMP rate); infrared recycler if BT and d ≤ 40 mm and dry; CC slab: epoxy/polymer mortar item flagged for engineer. Monsoon flag: standing water must be bailed; do not schedule CMBM surface layers in rain (IRC:SP:100 cl. 2645), patching allowed.
- Output: Measurement Book (MB) draft line items per work order, exportable CSV/PDF for e-Measurement (eMARG pattern).

### 1.7 Work orders & verification loop (`workorders/`)
- Jurisdiction router: `road_owner` polygons/ways (GHMC zone/circle/ward — pluggable 150/300 wards & 3-corporation split; R&B; NHAI; Cantonment) + CRMP package polygons → contractor; DLP window per package (5 yr CRMP; 6 months for standalone patch).
- SLA defaults: 24 h arterial in monsoon (GHMC charter), 72 h other, 7 days off-season; configurable.
- Field PWA: offline work-order list for the engineer's circle, before/after geo-time-stamped photos, cold-mix batch/lot no., bags used (compared with estimate → variance flag >25 %), Telugu/Hindi/English.
- Verification: automatic — ≥3 clean passes (no detection within 8 m in same way+direction with depth_below_plane < 10 mm) within 14 days after `repaired_reported` → `verified_closed`; manual QC sample 10 %. Payment flag only on `verified_closed`. Re-detection within DLP → `reopened`, contractor-liable debit-note draft. Patch durability analytics: survival curve per contractor/material/method/monsoon.
- Citizen intake: WhatsApp bot (Twilio/Meta Cloud API stub) + web form → observation with method `citizen_photo` (depth unknown) merged into cluster; public transparency page per ward.

### 1.8 Hardware BOM
- Bus Tier A: Android phone ₹10k + mount/fan/DC-DC ₹2k + IoT SIM ₹100/mo; or Jetson Orin Nano (industrial) ₹35–55k + IMX296 GS cam ₹8k + GNSS/IMU ₹3k + enclosure ₹5k.
- Van Tier B: Jetson Orin Nano + OAK-D Pro (₹31–35k) or ZED 2i (₹52–63k + GST) with polariser, pitch 20°, 8.33 ms exposure.
- Truth: 1 iPhone 15 Pro per zone (LiDAR scans, ≤5 m), straightedge + depth gauge, 1 m² painted square + cone for scale checks.
- Server: dev RTX 5080 (16 GB) handles ~12 depth frames/s at 518 px → ~1 M detections/day capacity; production NIC/MeghRaj GPU VM.

### 1.9 Backend/DB (`server/`)
Python 3.11 venv, FastAPI ≥0.128.1 + uvicorn, SQLAlchemy 2.0.x + GeoAlchemy2 (pin <2.1), psycopg 3, PostgreSQL 16/18 + PostGIS 3.4+/3.6 (local install, no docker), Redis + Celery (`gpu` queue, `--pool=solo`, batch 16), MinIO or local FS via boto3 S3 API, pyjwt+argon2, roles citizen/field_engineer/contractor/zonal_admin/super_admin scoped by `ulb_id`/`zone_id`.

APIs (FastAPI, `/api/v1`): `POST /ingest/upload-init|part|complete` (tus-like), `POST /ingest/detections` (batch JSON), `GET /potholes?bbox&status&min_priority&ulb`, `GET /potholes/{id}` (measurements, images, history), `GET /tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt` (ST_AsMVT, H3-bucketed at z<13), `POST /measure` (upload image + calib → measurement; demo endpoint), `POST /workorders/plan` (pothole ids → material plan), `PATCH /workorders/{id}` (field update + photos), `GET /analytics/ward|contractor|material`, `POST /citizen/report`, `GET /export/geojson|csv`, `GET /calib/{device}/cert`, `POST /truth/measurements`.

### 1.10 Dashboard & field PWA (`web/`)
React 19 + Vite + MapLibre GL (self-hosted PMTiles Telangana basemap) + TanStack Query + Zustand + i18next (te/hi/en, Noto Sans Telugu/Devanagari) + vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox background sync, Dexie queue). Views: live map (clusters/H3 heat, severity colours), pothole detail (image, mask, depth profile cross-section, volume with ±, history), priority queue, work-order board, contractor scorecard (repairs, median days, recurrence %, bags variance), material forecast per circle (bags/week from backlog + monsoon), IRC:82 stretch rating, calibration status per bus, public transparency page. Low bandwidth: WebP thumbs ≤20 KB, brotli, offline tile pack per circle.

### 1.11 Demo path on dev machine (real public data)
Download RDD2022_India.zip, eYantra Kaggle set, BharatPotHole; train YOLO26s-seg (~1 h on 5080); run DA3METRIC-LARGE depth on eYantra/RDD frames with assumed dashcam intrinsics (fx≈ image_width·1.0 for 720p phone at ~60° HFOV, h=1.4 m) → measurements with wide sigma; synthesize trips by assigning frames to real Hyderabad TGSRTC GTFS route shapes (mdb-3361) with jittered GPS; map-match on OSRM over Geofabrik southern-zone Telangana clip; dedup, priority with GTFS stops + OSM schools/hospitals; produce work orders and bag counts; dashboard over Hyderabad. A calibrated accuracy demo: print checkerboard, film a staged "pothole" (foam-board hole of known depth) with any phone, run full pipeline, show measured vs true depth.
