depth_method:
Goal: per-pothole max/mean depth (mm), area (m²), volume (L) with stated uncertainty, from a single calibrated vehicle camera, corroborated by IMU, with stereo and manual tiers sharing the same geometry.

1. Calibration (per device, stored cert): intrinsics K=(fx,fy,cx,cy)+distortion from a 9×6 checkerboard (30–40 mm squares, 20 poses, reprojection <0.3 px); extrinsics at the depot: tape-measured camera height h_true, pitch/roll/yaw from solvePnP on 4 cones at 3/5/8/12 m; known-object check (1 m² painted square or 750 mm IRC cone at 5 m must reconstruct within 5 %). Online per trip: vanishing-point pitch/yaw check, lane-width prior (3.5 m ± 0.25 on marked arterials only), RANSAC plane height vs h_true → drift alert >5 %.

2. Metric depth prediction: undistort frame; run Depth Anything 3 METRIC-LARGE (`depth-anything/DA3METRIC-LARGE`, Apache-2.0) with the calibrated fx: `Z_metric = fx_px · net_out / 300` (convention to be validated empirically on the staged target — code keeps `scale_convention` configurable). Fallbacks: `depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Metric-VKITTI-Base`, Metric3D v2 ViT-S ONNX (`onnx-community/metric3d-vit-small`, BSD) for Jetson. Back-project to a point cloud: X=(u−cx)Z/fx, Y=(v−cy)Z/fy.

3. Road plane and scale lock: take road pixels (road seg from YOLO road class or lower-image band minus all detection masks dilated 20 px) in the 3–12 m range band; open3d `segment_plane(distance_threshold=0.015, ransac_n=3, num_iterations=1000)` → plane n·p + d = 0, camera height ĥ = |d|. Scale factor s = h_true / ĥ; multiply all Z by s (cancels monocular absolute-scale error, which is 5–30 % on an unseen dashcam). Rotate cloud so plane normal = +Y (road frame). Residual plane RMS stored (`plane_rms_mm`, reject frame if >15 mm — crowned/rutted road handled by fitting a local quadratic surface `y = a + bx + cz + dx² + ez² + fxz` to the ring region 0.3–1.0 m around the mask instead of the global plane).

4. Pothole geometry: for each mask pixel i, depth below surface δ_i = (surface_height(x_i,z_i) − y_i), clipped at ≥0; drop pixels with model-confidence < threshold. Per-pixel ground footprint a_i = (Z_i/fx)(Z_i/fy)/cos θ_i (θ = ray angle to plane normal) — the IPM footprint. Report: depth_max = max δ (noise-prone), depth_p95, depth_mean = Σδ_i a_i / Σa_i, area A = Σa_i, volume V = Σ δ_i a_i, length/width = extent of projected mask on plane along/across travel, lane_offset = lateral mask centroid. IRC:82 cl. 7.5.3.4 severity from depth_p95 and width: Small ≤25 mm & ~200 mm, Medium 25–50 mm or ~500 mm, Large >50 mm or >500 mm (depth governs when inconsistent).

5. Uncertainty: per-pixel depth σ_Z ≈ k·Z² (k fitted on the truth set, initial k such that σ_Z = 4 cm at 10 m) propagated: σ_δ ≈ sqrt(σ_Z²·sin²θ + plane_rms²), σ_A ≈ 2A·σ_Z/Z, σ_V ≈ sqrt((σ_δ/δ̄)² + (σ_A/A)²)·V. Quality score from range, plane RMS, mask conf, blur metric (Laplacian variance), illumination. Expected (to be measured, no published bus-mounted GT exists): single frame at 8–15 m ±10–25 mm depth / ±20–40 % volume; fused ±5–15 mm / ±15–25 %.

6. Multi-frame fusion: BoT-SORT track across the approach; keep frames in 3–12 m; Kalman/inverse-variance weighted fusion of depth_p95, A, V with weights 1/σ² (closest 3–6 m frames dominate); fused σ reported; outlier frames (jump >3σ) dropped.

7. IMU corroboration: when the wheel path crosses the pothole (lane_offset within wheel track ±0.3 m), find z-accel jolt in ±0.5 s of predicted pass time; 1-DoF quarter-car model with per-vehicle gain g_v (fitted on truth set) → imu_depth_mm (~15 % error literature). Used to (a) confirm existence (filters shadows/wet-patch FPs), (b) override to `water_filled` depth lower bound, (c) night/rain fallback where camera depth quality < threshold.

8. Water-filled potholes: flag if class `pothole_water`, or RGB detector fires but δ_p95 < 8 mm with specular/low-texture mask, or polarised-stereo (Tier B) disagreement. Set `depth = unknown`, `water_filled = true`, severity by area + IMU + complaint count; schedule re-measurement after 48 h dry or by inspection van. Never report a water surface as pothole floor.

9. Tier B stereo (vans, billing grade): OAK-D Pro / ZED 2i (polariser, pitch 20°, ≤8.33 ms exposure, Zhang calibration); depth from the device's SGBM/NN at 0.5–8 m; same steps 3–6 (plane fit still applied to remove tilt and lock scale with h_true). Target ±12 % depth at 40 km/h per ISPRS 2025.

10. Ground truth & certification: inspectors measure 50–100 potholes per zone with 1.2 m straightedge + depth gauge (IRC manual) and iPhone LiDAR mesh (volume ±5 %); `measure/truth.py` computes depth MAE and volume MAPE per range bin per device, fits k and g_v, and issues a per-bus calibration certificate; measurements from an uncertified device are usable for prioritisation but not for Measurement Book billing.

Dev-machine validation plan: staged foam-board potholes of known depth (20/40/70 mm) and area filmed with a checkerboard-calibrated phone at h=1.4 m, 5–12 m, moving; run the full chain and report error table — this is the credibility artefact for the jury.
key_tradeoffs:
- Monocular (cheap, every bus) vs stereo (accurate ≤8 m, ₹30–60k, Jetson host) vs LiDAR (accurate, costly): chose monocular + height-scale as the fleet default with explicit uncertainty, stereo on a few municipal vans for billing-grade numbers, phone-LiDAR for truth. Same geometry code, one schema with `method` + sigma, so quality is auditable instead of pretending all numbers are equal.
- Depth server-side vs on-edge: server-side keeps bus kits cheap (phone), lets models improve retroactively over archived crops, costs bandwidth (~150 KB/detection, <1 GB/bus/month) and adds latency (minutes, acceptable vs 24-h SLA). Jetson vans run depth locally for stereo.
- YOLO26-seg (fastest, NMS-free, AGPL) vs RF-DETR-Seg (Apache, better domain shift, slower): YOLO26 on edge for the prototype, RF-DETR as server verifier/teacher; production edge needs an Ultralytics Enterprise licence or a swap to RF-DETR-Seg-Nano — flagged, not hidden.
- DA3METRIC-LARGE (Apache, focal-aware, no published outdoor AbsRel) vs DA2-Metric-VKITTI (known KITTI numbers, fixed canonical camera) vs Metric3D v2 (BSD, heavy): the plane-fit height rescale makes absolute model scale largely irrelevant, so we pick the best relative-geometry model (DA3) and keep backends swappable; benchmark all three on the staged truth set.
- Integrated volume + IRC square-cut vs cuboid L×W×D: integrated is 2–4× lower material (saves money, matches reality) but the repair really cuts a rectangle to sound material, so we bill cut-area × design depth with the integrated volume stored for auditing — defensible to R&B engineers.
- Confirm on ≥2 passes vs act on first sighting: fewer FPs and real dedup at the cost of a few hours' delay — buses repeat routes many times a day, so delay is small; citizen report counts as a pass.
- Python 3.11 venv (works now, torch cu128 on RTX 5080) vs Python 3.14 (newest, wheel gaps for rfdetr/onnxruntime/tensorrt): use 3.11 now.
- PostGIS-only vs TimescaleDB: PostGIS + monthly partitions + BRIN suffices; IMU raw stays as blobs in object storage.
- OSRM (fast to set up) vs Valhalla Meili (better map-matching knobs): OSRM for demo, Valhalla for production.
- Fixed IRC-style weights vs learned prioritisation: fixed, transparent, per-ULB editable weights (govt auditability) with the data model to learn later.
- Phone kit vs Jetson kit on buses: phone is ₹10k and proven (RoadMetrics/vialytics) but throttles above 45 °C; Jetson is robust but ₹40k+ — pilot both on 20 buses and decide by uptime.
risks:
- Monocular depth accuracy on real bus footage is unproven (no published bus-mounted GT study); mitigation: uncertainty reporting, multi-frame fusion, stereo tier for billing, early truth campaign (50–100 potholes) before claiming numbers; demo accuracy on staged targets.
- DA3METRIC scale convention (×focal vs ×focal/300) is disputed; mitigation: plane-height rescale makes it moot, and it is validated on the staged target on day 1.
- Water-filled potholes (the monsoon case) cannot be depth-measured monocularly; design reports `unknown` with IMU/area-based severity; polarised stereo and dry re-measurement are the fallbacks.
- Motion blur, night, dust, heavy rain degrade detection (expect 20–30 % more misses at dusk); mitigation: ≤8 ms exposure/global shutter on Jetson kits, frame quality gating, more passes.
- GPS 5–15 m error in Hyderabad canyons and multi-lane ambiguity; mitigation: map-match + IPM ground-point offset + lane_offset + DBSCAN 8 m; residual mis-assignment on parallel service roads remains.
- Licensing: YOLO26 AGPL, eYantra GPL-2, UniDepth/Depth Pro NC; mitigation: Apache paths (RF-DETR-Seg, DA3METRIC, Metric3D) and prototype-only use of GPL data, documented.
- Dataset domain gap (RDD India = Delhi/Haryana plains; no Telangana set); mitigation: IDD Hyderabad negatives, self-collected TGSRTC footage pseudo-labelled by the teacher, active learning.
- Hardware heat (phones shut down >45 °C on dashboards; Jetson dev kit 0–35 °C); mitigation: industrial carriers, shaded mounts, fans, uptime telemetry.
- Jurisdiction/contract data (road owner, CRMP package polygons, DLP text) is not public; mitigation: pluggable `road_owner`/`package` layers with admin upload, defaults from OSM and news-sourced package lists.
- Ward boundaries changed in 2026 (150 vs 300 wards, three corporations); mitigation: ward layer is a swappable GeoJSON with validity dates.
- Python-ecosystem drift (rfdetr/onnxruntime on new Python, SQLAlchemy 2.1 vs GeoAlchemy2): pin to 3.11 venv and SQLAlchemy 2.0.x.
- Governance adoption risk (contractor liability features face pushback): keep payment linkage configurable per ULB; start with transparency reports.
- Hackathon-time risk: the full stack is large; the build order front-loads the measurement demo so a credible partial deliverable exists by step 6.
